summary: Fixed in #710 (60633eff3), which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. LazyRightPanel no longer wraps every mode in a pool provider. Only DiffPanel (review), the PR FilesTab and the read-only DiffsFile branch of PreviewPanel lease the pool. On desktop, text files go straight to the edit-mode editor, because the edit session snapshot is created synchronously in the constructor. That editor gates the pool off anyway (FileRenderer checks !editSessionActive), so files, terminal, launcher, agents, simulator and render modes start no workers. A module-level, lease-counted owner keeps the pool after close, with a 3 min idle grace (30 s while hidden), so grammars and AST caches survive close, reopen and thread switches. Pool size is now clamp(floor(cores/4), 1, 2) instead of min(3, floor(cores/3)). Review intent (hover, focus, shortcut or open) prewarms the workers. Non-intent idle preloads only fetch code. Unit and browser tests cover the owner lifecycle, provider reuse across remounts, and intent-only prewarm. I found no other @pierre/diffs pool consumer outside a provider. The remaining gaps are minor polish.

evidence.note: LazyRightPanel has no DiffWorkerPoolProvider. The old f1be4abc7 code wrapped every mode. It is mounted only while open or during the delayed unmount (ChatRightPanel.tsx:146-149, 252).
DiffPanel wraps itself, so the lease lives only while review is mounted. It is rendered only in the review gate (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1499-1501).
The PR files surface wraps itself. PullRequestReader.tsx:41 renders FilesTab, and DiffFileSection is only reached through PullRequestDiffStream inside FilesTab.

Editable text uses PreviewFileEditor (no provider). Only the read-only DiffsFile fallback (phone tier, mixed line endings, no session) is wrapped. PreviewFileEditSession.ts:61 creates the session snapshot synchronously, so desktop never flashes through the DiffsFile branch.
The pool is skipped while editSessionActive. Taking the pool context away from the editor path does not move work onto the main thread.
Lease-counted owner with a 3 min / 30 s hidden idle grace. Pool size is clamp(floor(cores/4), 1, 2).
Single app-lifetime owner bound to WorkerPoolManager, with a visibilitychange listener and get/acquire/prewarm exports.
Renders WorkerPoolContext.Provider directly. Resolves the pool in the useState initializer, leases it in an effect and re-syncs if the pool was retired.
Only intent (hover, focus, shortcut, open) on review calls prewarmDiffWorkerPool(). Idle preload only imports the module.
Tests cover shared lease, reopen within grace, termination after grace, the hidden grace, retiring an unleased pool, double release and pool sizing.
Browser test: the same pool is reused across a provider unmount and remount.
Only an intent warms the workers.

fixDefects: Minor, low impact. (1) Theme drift while the pool idles: owner.get(themeName) at diffWorkerPoolOwner.ts:79-87 ignores themeName when a pool already exists. Suppose the app theme flips (manual or OS-driven) while no provider is mounted, and review reopens within the 3 min grace. The FileDiff instances are then created in the commit's ref callbacks with the stale pool theme. DiffWorkerThemeSync's passive useEffect (DiffWorkerPoolProvider.tsx:10-26) only calls setRenderOptions afterwards. That call clears diffCache and fileCache and invalidates tasks (WorkerPoolManager.js:102-140), so the reopen briefly shows the old theme colours, wastes one round of worker highlighting and loses the warm cache for that open. The old per-open provider always created the pool with the current theme. (2) Proposal item 4 is only partly done. Prewarm starts the workers and the theme, but it does not call primeFileHighlightCache with a snippet in the thread's dominant language, and there is no requestIdleCallback prewarm when a thread with turnDiffSummaries renders. The first diff in a fresh pool still compiles its grammar on demand. (3) Proposal item 3 is only partly followed: hosts with 8 or more cores get 2 workers, not a default of 1. That is a deliberate trade-off for large patches.
implementationSketch: Optional polish. (1) Theme drift: in DiffWorkerPoolProvider's useState initializer, or in diffWorkerPool.getDiffWorkerPool, compare pool.getDiffRenderOptions().theme with the requested themeName when the owner returns an existing pool. If they differ, fire pool.setRenderOptions({...current, theme}) before the children commit. Alternatively, subscribe the owner to the theme store (useTheme's root class toggle) so an idle pool re-themes eagerly. Test: in DiffWorkerPoolProvider.browser.tsx, mount with dark, unmount, switch to light, remount, and assert getDiffRenderOptions().theme === light before the first highlight result. A unit test in diffWorkerPoolOwner.test.ts can cover a get() theme-mismatch hook. (2) Grammar prime: in prewarmDiffWorkerPool, accept an optional language hint (dominant extension from the active thread's latest turnDiffSummaries files) and call pool.primeFileHighlightCache({name: `prewarm.${ext}`, contents: '\n', cacheKey: `prewarm:${ext}`}). Optionally schedule it from scheduleIdleTask once a thread with turn diffs renders, honouring saveData. Extend workspacePanelPreload.test.ts to assert the hint is passed. (3) Pool size: if memory matters more than large-patch throughput, change MAX or the divisor in resolveDiffWorkerPoolSize to default to 1, or size it from the first lease's file count. Update the sizing test.
decisionReason: Client-only web perf polish. It does not touch auth, E2EE, the hosted lifecycle or the Hub protocol.
correction: None of substance. The auditor's DONE holds. I add one minor edge the auditor missed: a stale theme on reopen after a theme switch while the pool is idle. The phone or no-session DiffsFile path is correctly wrapped, and the desktop editor path never touches the pool.
